title: His musical brothers, sister and singing father
summary: Brothers Teddy, Jay (Ruben) and Herbert play piano or drums, his sister played church piano, and their father had them sing syllables at the piano.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Let me see, according to Chilton it said
two of your brothers were piano players, right?
Yes, Teddy and Jay, June, or Ruben. Teddy played with Roy Eldridge around Chicago for a while. Then Jay has played with oh, different groups around, this Miss Rhapsody in Newark, New Jersey.
What was that?

She was a singer, and he used to arrange for her and things, then Jay was with my band on the African tour and then at the Metropole when I was at the Metropole. And he's worked quite a bit around with different musicians, you know, free-lancing, but I can speak very well about him, the time that he spent with me; see he was with me oh four, five years with my band.
In the late '50s, early '60s.
Yes, then he also did the African tour with me.
Are they younger or older than you?
They were younger.
Are they both still alive?
No, Ruben passed on in 1975. And the rest of them are living, Ted
Teddy's alive.
Yeah, and then I have another youngest brother, Herbert. He plays drums also. He's in Asbury Park, New Jersey.
Does he play professionally?

Yes, sort of, he wasn't too interested in the drums, you know. He would play a little and then neglect them for a while and you just can't become professional when you put your instrument down like that and not play it. He wasn't interested in it that much, I would say. He'd play enough just to play and say that he was playing drums.
Three out of four in one family isn't bad.

Then I have a sister, she played piano. But not professionally. Played in church. She studied piano for years I guess this is when all of us were quite young. My father used to sing. He used to get us all around the piano and we would do a lot of, what would you call that, there's a word there that I want where we used to exercise-- syllabals. We used to exercise (SINGING) ....
Do re me fa sol.

Yeah, yeah, and believe it or not I used to sing soprano. You wouldn't believe that now because I have a bass voice, but all of us used to get around and sing things like that, syllables. And that's how, well I would say it was a musical family, really.
Sounds like it.
Yes. At the beginning, and of course I pursued mine and Ruben he did also, and also Ted. Herb is the only one that didn't take it too serious. My sister,
she played in churches and things of that nature. And that was it.
